s2.p1: The **Namibia Amateur DanceSport Association** was founded in 2007. In 2008 it joined the world body, IDSF, as member ==number 87==.
s2.p2: In 2013 the WDSF moved to end it over unpaid fees. Today Namibia is a provisional member, and Windhoek’s **Dance Domain** teaches ballroom.

s3.p: won by **Dance Domain Windhoek** at the 2016 Dance Domain Open, a ballroom, Latin and Pro/Am event: 42 gold, 37 silver and 38 bronze.

s4.p1: Namibia picks its **first national dancesport team**: 14 dancers bound for Sun City, South Africa, to compete in ballroom and Latin.
s4.p2: More than ==21 countries== were expected. Before leaving, the team received Namibia’s **national sport colours** for the first time.

s5.name: ONDJONGO
s5.p: Men and women stand in a **semicircle**: clapping, stomping, quick footwork. A celebration dance, performed at any social celebration.

s5.name: NAMA STAP
s5.p: “The dancing steps of the Nama.” Women sway softly; men **stamp hard** to show they protect them. Some moves mimic an ostrich guarding its chicks.

s6.p: Ju/’hoansi women dance in a semicircle, passing a ball made from a **wild melon** tuber. A man tries to catch it. When he does, the game stops.

s7.p: Newly formed **Dance Sport Namibia** joins the Olympic committee: dance is now a sport code. Its founder said Namibia was “15 years behind” in seeing dance as sport.
s7.p2: Windhoek’s **Xallamo Gariseb** wins the first Red Bull Dance Your Style Namibia, earning a place at the World Final in Zürich.
